proposer.mechanism: EWMA-weighted signed aggressor flow gate (stand-alone): replace base AFG's rectangular 10s window with an exponentially-decayed flow estimator. Compute weighted_flow = sum(signed_vol_i * exp(-(t_order - t_i)/tau)) over prints with ts_event in (t_order - 10s, t_order]. Skip BUY when weighted_flow <= -2.0, skip SELL when weighted_flow >= +2.0. Anti-cascade via _position_flat=True after skip. Reduce-only always submits.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: The rectangular window treats 9.9s-old prints identically to 0.1s-old prints; adverse-selection decays rapidly so recency-weighted flow is a sharper conditioner.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Slippage is 0 in this simulator; only cost is foregone P&L from skipping good entries. Recency weighting reduces false-positive skips on stale flow bursts.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate base — replaces uniform window with EWMA. Distinct from r1-r4.
proposer.alternatives_considered: Linear decay (less smooth); shorter window with flat weights (less info); combining with r2's chain (deferred to round 2 if criticized).

objections.text: Alternative not considered: r2 (chain state machine) is the empirical winner (+600% vs base, sharpe 5.27). A stand-alone EWMA gate replaces r2's mechanism instead of building on it. A clearly stronger approach is to combine EWMA flow estimator WITH r2's directional-chain — extending the winning mechanism along the orthogonal decay dimension.
Decay constant tau is a free parameter without principled rationale. Needs to be tied to the empirical 10s window or oracle's 30s horizon.
EWMA weighted sum has different magnitude scale than raw window sum, so threshold 2.0 may not translate directly — may need rescaling.

suggested_alternatives: Combine EWMA decay with r2's directional-chain state machine; set tau = window_seconds/2 = 5s for principled half-life choice.
criticizer.reasoning: Hypothesis is sound but ignores the empirical winner (r2) and underspecifies the decay parameter.

proposer.mechanism: EWMA-weighted signed flow + r2 directional-chain. Compute weighted_flow at order time using exp(-(t_order - t_i)/tau) with tau=5s. Skip threshold lowered to 1.5 to preserve approximately the same skip rate as base/r2 (since EWMA weighted sum is ~75% of raw uniform sum for uniformly-distributed prints over 10s with tau=5s). Chain state machine from r2 preserved verbatim: max_consecutive_skips=3, direction-change force-submits, reduce-only always submits.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Same as r1 — recency-weighting sharpens adverse-flow detection. Combined with r2's chain to preserve the empirical winner's structure.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Sharper gate plus the proven chain logic should yield more accurate skip decisions than r2's flat-weighted flow.
proposer.builds_on: afg-pc-r2 + EWMA weighting; addresses r1 criticism #1.
proposer.alternatives_considered: Keep threshold at 2.0 (rejected — would change effective skip rate); use tau tied to oracle horizon=30s (rejected — too long, defeats recency emphasis).
proposer.revision_notes: Combined with r2 chain (addresses MAJOR #1). Set tau=window/2=5s with principled half-life rationale (addresses MAJOR #2). Rescaled threshold to 1.5 to preserve skip rate (addresses MINOR #3).

objections.text: Overfitting risk: r2's empirical success was tuned to threshold=2.0 and max_skips=3. By simultaneously changing the weighting function AND the threshold to 1.5, we tune two coupled knobs and can't attribute any P&L change to either independently. A cleaner ablation is to keep threshold=2.0 — let the weighting change be the single isolated variable. This is more falsifiable: if it improves, decay-weighting alone is the cause; if it hurts, decay-weighting alone is the problem.

EWMA requires O(N) per decision instead of O(1) since per-print weight depends on current order timestamp. Need to confirm this is fine — at ~100-1000 prints in 10s for MES, the cost is negligible per decision.

suggested_alternatives: Hold flow_threshold=2.0 constant; let the decay function be the only change vs r2.
criticizer.reasoning: Mechanism is right but threshold rescaling introduces coupled-variable confounding. Isolate decay as the sole change.

proposer.mechanism: Time-decayed AFG with r2 chain state machine (single-variable ablation vs r2). At each open-order decision, compute weighted_flow = sum(signed_vol_i * exp(-(t_order - t_i)/tau_ns)) over all flow_deque entries with ts_event in (t_order - 10s, t_order], where tau = 5s (half-life ~= 3.47s). Skip BUY when weighted_flow <= -2.0, skip SELL when weighted_flow >= +2.0 (threshold IDENTICAL to base/r2). Directional-chain state machine preserved VERBATIM from r2: max_consecutive_skips=3, direction-change immediately force-submits and resets chain, reduce-only always submits, first-signal warm-up unconditional submit. Trade-tick subscription and deque maintenance identical to r2; only the gate evaluation function changes from raw _net_flow comparison to weighted recomputation at order time. Look-ahead-free: only prints with ts_event <= order.ts_init contribute.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: The base rectangular window treats a 9.9s-old print identically to a 0.1s-old print, but adverse-selection from aggressor flow decays rapidly — what aggressors did 8 seconds ago is mostly already priced in. Recency weighting sharpens the gate to respond to currently-active flow rather than averaged stale flow, while still using older prints as context (down-weighted, not discarded).
proposer.why_survives_costs: Slippage is 0 in this simulator (zero fill-cost model); the only cost is foregone P&L from over-skipping. With threshold and chain held constant at r2's values, decay-weighting should reduce two failure modes: (a) false-positive skips when a stale 8s-old burst has already reversed; (b) false-negative submits when fresh adverse flow is diluted by older neutral flow in the unweighted sum. Net effect: more accurate skip targeting at approximately the same skip rate.
proposer.builds_on: afg-pc-r2 (the empirical winner). Sole change: rectangular weighting -> EWMA weighting at gate evaluation. All other r2 mechanics preserved verbatim: chain state machine, max_consecutive_skips=3, flow_threshold=2.0, window_seconds=10.0, reduce-only, first-signal warm-up, on_reset semantics.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Linear/triangular decay — qualitatively similar but less smooth; exponential is the standard microstructure recency-weighting choice. (b) tau=window (10s) — too long, weights only ~37% drop at window boundary; defeats recency emphasis. (c) tau=1s — too short, effectively ignores anything older than 3s. (d) tau=window/2=5s — principled compromise: half-life ~3.5s gives strong recency emphasis while preserving meaningful context from the older half of the window. (e) Threshold rescaling — rejected per round-2 criticism to keep the ablation clean.
proposer.revision_notes: R2 introduced threshold/decay coupling. R3 isolates decay as the sole change vs r2: threshold=2.0 held constant, chain state machine identical, max_consecutive_skips=3 unchanged. Pure single-variable test of the decay-weighting hypothesis. O(N) eval cost acknowledged and accepted (~100-1000 prints per decision; trivial for MES).

criticizer.reasoning: Single-variable ablation of the empirical winner along a principled microstructure dimension (recency-weighting). Logically coherent, no look-ahead, no near-duplicate of prior runs, no clearly stronger untried alternative remains.
